content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) published consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services in 2016 and updated them in 2019 to include recommendations for dual HIV/syphilis rapid diagnostic tests as the first test in antenatal care. 2. WHO released guidelines in 2016 for the treatment of Treponema pallidum (syphilis) and in 2020 for the prevention of mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B virus through antiviral prophylaxis during pregnancy. 3. WHO emphasizes key principles in its guidelines, including human rights, gender equality, equity and inclusion, medical ethics, universal health coverage, evidence-based public health, and community-led responses by key populations. 4. Studies such as those by Coomes et al. (2022) and others have explored youth-centered digital health interventions and frameworks for planning and implementing solutions with and for young people. 5. WHO has issued guidelines on self-care interventions for health and well-being (2021), management of symptomatic sexually transmitted infections (2021), and hepatitis B and C testing (2017). 6. Research by Rodger et al. (2016) and Cohen et al. (2011) has demonstrated that suppressive antiretroviral therapy in HIV-positive individuals significantly reduces the risk of HIV transmission in serodifferent couples. 7. Studies like Bavinton et al. (2018) have shown that viral suppression in serodiscordant male couples effectively prevents HIV transmission, as confirmed by international cohort studies. 8. WHO has developed modules on tuberculosis (TB) screening, treatment, and prevention, including drug-resistant TB treatment (2020) and TB preventive treatment (2020). 9. WHO guidelines for the care and treatment of chronic hepatitis C (2018) and hepatitis B (2015) provide comprehensive recommendations for managing these infections. 10. Research by Grulich et al. (2007) highlights the increased incidence of cancers in people with HIV/AIDS compared to immunosuppressed transplant recipients. 11. WHO's position paper on human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines (2017) underscores their importance in preventing HPV-related diseases. 12. WHO guidelines on cervical cancer prevention (2021) include recommendations for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions, particularly among women living with HIV. 13. WHO's abortion care guideline (2022) provides evidence-based recommendations for safe abortion practices. 14. The WHO mental health gap action programme (mhGAP) (2016) offers guidance for managing mental, neurological, and substance use disorders in non-specialized health settings. 15. The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989) establishes the framework for protecting children's rights globally. 16. Studies like those by Rashti et al. (2020) and Degenhardt et al. (2017) examine the global prevalence of hepatitis B and C co-infections among people who inject drugs and female sex workers living with HIV/AIDS. 17. Research by Larney et al. (2013) and others has investigated the incidence and prevalence of hepatitis C in prisons and other closed settings, emphasizing the need for integrated care. 18. WHO guidelines on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, and care for key populations (2021) stress the importance of community-led responses and evidence-based interventions. 19. Studies on transgender health, such as those by Reisner et al. (2016) and Wirtz et al. (2020), highlight the need for integrated, gender-affirming clinical care and research to address violence and discrimination. 20. Research on the quality of life of transgender individuals, such as by Nobil et al. (2018), underscores the importance of addressing stigma and providing comprehensive healthcare. 21. WHO's International Classification of Diseases (ICD-11) (2019) provides a standardized framework for diagnosing and classifying diseases and related health problems. 22. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) has published reports on prisons and health, including the Nelson Mandela Rules (2016) and comprehensive HIV prevention packages for prisoners (2020). 23. Studies like those by Nguyen et al. (2019) and Vannakit et al. (2020) demonstrate the effectiveness of community-led HIV testing services and health interventions in concentrated epidemic settings. 24. Research by Reza-Paul et al. (2019) evaluates community-led integrated HIV and sexual and reproductive health services for sex workers, emphasizing the importance of mixed-methods approaches.
